message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need to know | |---------|-----------------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands when you finish a round. | | **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck). | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”, two “Draw Two”) + 4 “Wild” + 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Turn the top card of the draw pile face‑up to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two”, the first player draws two and loses a turn). | | **Turn Order** | Players sit in a circle. The first turn goes to the player left of the dealer. “Reverse” flips the direction. | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either:
• the color of the top discard card, **or**
• the number/symbol of the top discard card.
• A Wild card can be played on any card. | | **Special Cards** | | **Effect** | | **Skip** | Next player loses their turn. | | **Reverse** | Reverses play direction. (With 2 players, it acts like a Skip.) | | **Draw Two** | Next player draws two cards and loses their turn. | | **Wild** | You choose the new color. | | **Wild Draw Four** | You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. **Must be played only if you have no other playable card** (see “Uno Challenge” below). | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, the round ends. | | **Scoring** | • Add up the point values of the cards left in each opponent’s hand:
 • Number cards = face value.
 • Skip, Reverse, Draw Two = 20 points.
 • Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points.
• The winner of the round receives those points. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach 500 points (or your chosen target) wins. | --- ### Common House Variations | Variation | What it changes | |-----------|-----------------| | **“Draw 4” rule** | Some players allow a Wild Draw Four to be played even if you have a matching color card. | | **“Uno Challenge”** | If a player plays a Wild Draw Four but has a playable card, the next player can challenge. If the challenger is right, the original player must draw 4 cards; if wrong, the challenger draws 6. | | **“Stacking”** | Allow players to stack Draw Two or Draw Four cards (e.g., if you play a Draw Two, the next player can play another Draw Two to pass the penalty). | | **“No Draw”** | Instead of drawing, a player must skip their turn if they cannot play. | | **“Play to 200”** | Shorter game: first to 200 points wins. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of colors** – If you’re low on a particular color, try to play it early to avoid being stuck later. 2. **Use Wilds strategically** – Save them for when you’re about to run out of playable cards or to change the color to something you have many of. 3. **Watch opponents’ “UNO” calls** – If someone says “UNO” and you’re close to finishing, you might want to play a Skip or Draw Two to stop them. 4. **Remember the penalty** – If you forget to say “UNO” and get caught, you’ll have to draw two cards, which can be a big setback. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
